tracks.title: Tracks
tracks.full: Ten tracks are loaded, the most the app holds. Remove one to add another.
track.limit: Three tracks are showing. Hide one to show this one.
measure.speed.long: How fast you were moving at each fix. Taken from the file when the logger records speed, otherwise worked out from the distance and time between fixes.
measure.ele.long: Height above sea level, as the logger recorded it. GPS height is less precise than position, so expect it to wander by several meters.
measure.grade.long: How steep the track is, uphill or downhill: the change in elevation over about {distance} of track, as a percentage.
measure.hdop.long: Horizontal dilution of precision: how much the layout of the satellites in the sky magnifies position errors. Lower is better. Below 2, the satellites were well spread out; higher values mean fixes may be further off.
measure.sats.long: How many satellites the logger used for each fix. A fix needs at least four; more usually means a steadier position.
measure.fix.long: Whether each fix was a plain GPS fix, or one corrected with help from SBAS satellites or another correction service, which usually makes it more accurate.
measure.hdop.relativeNote: This file's HDOP values don't behave like standard HDOP, so the track is ranked against itself, from its best quarter of fixes to its worst.
halo.hint.hdopRelative: Wider halo: weaker fix for this logger

problem.truncated.title: Last line cut off
problem.truncated.body: Line {line} stops after {chars} characters, without a line break: the logger probably stopped mid-write. That line was skipped; the {kept} fixes before it loaded.
problem.checksum.body: Starting at line {line}. They were skipped, since their numbers can't be trusted.
problem.glued.body: Starting at line {line}, sentences share a line with no break between them. They were split and read separately.
problem.garbage.body: Starting at line {line}, characters that never appear in NMEA were found and removed.
problem.badRows.body: Starting at line {line}, rows with the wrong number of fields were skipped.
problem.backwards.body: Starting at line {line}. They were left out, so the track only moves forward in time.
problem.jump.body: Starting at line {line}, a fix sits farther from its neighbors than anything could travel. It was left out.
problem.unclosed.title: File ends early
problem.unclosed.body: The file stops before its closing tags, probably because it was cut off while being saved. The {kept} fixes before that point loaded.
problem.badXml.title: Damaged markup
problem.badXml.body: Line {line} has a tag that can't be read. Reading stopped there; the {kept} fixes before it loaded.
problem.noFixes.title: No fixes
problem.noFixes.body: The file has no fixes with both a time and a position.
note.speedUnitInferred: The file doesn't say which unit its speed uses; the numbers match {unit}.
note.speedUnitGuess: The file doesn't say which unit its speed uses, and comparing it with the positions didn't settle it, so it was read as {unit}. Change that under “Speed unit of the file”.
note.speedUnitChosen: The file doesn't say which unit its speed uses; you picked {unit}.
note.speedDerived: The file has no speed, so speed is worked out from positions and times.
note.hdopRelative: HDOP values don't behave like standard HDOP, so HDOP colors rank fixes within this track.

note.void.one: 1 fix without a position was skipped.
note.void.other: {n} fixes without a position were skipped.

note.timeless.one: 1 fix without a time was skipped.
note.timeless.other: {n} fixes without a time were skipped.

note.noZone: Times in the file have no time zone, so they were first read as UTC. Change that under “Time zone of the file”.
note.noDate: The file has no dates, only times of day.

note.timelessWaypoints.one: 1 waypoint without a time was left off the map.
note.timelessWaypoints.other: {n} waypoints without a time were left off the map.

note.gaps.other: {n} gaps without fixes; the longest is {longest} s.

note.eleZero: Elevation is 0 at every fix, a placeholder rather than a measurement, so it is left out.

note.zeroSatsStale.one: {count} fixes report 0 satellites used; 1 of them repeats the previous position.
note.zeroSatsStale.other: {count} fixes report 0 satellites used; {n} of them repeat the previous position.

note.zeroSatsAllStale.one: 1 fix reports 0 satellites used and repeats the previous position.
note.zeroSatsAllStale.other: {n} fixes report 0 satellites used; all of them repeat the previous position.

computed.label: Computed by the app
computed.distance: Adds up the straight-line distances between consecutive fixes. Jumps across gaps are left out.
computed.duration: The time from the first fix to the last.
computed.moving: The time spent moving faster than {speed}. Stops and gaps are left out.
computed.avgSpeed: The distance divided by the moving time.
computed.maxSpeed: The highest speed at any single fix.
computed.speedDerived: This file has no speed, so speed is worked out from the distance and time between neighboring fixes.
computed.grade: Worked out from elevation: the change in height over about {distance} of track, after averaging the GPS height over {s} seconds to calm its noise. Approximate.
computed.climb: The total of the uphill stretches, from GPS height averaged over {s} seconds. Rises smaller than {height} count as noise. Approximate.
computed.eleRange: The lowest and highest elevation recorded in the file.
computed.medianHdop: The middle value of the file's HDOP readings.
computed.medianSats: The middle value of the file's satellite counts.
computed.corrected: The share of fixes the file marks as corrected.
computed.ellipsoid: Elevation plus the geoid separation the file reports: the height above the WGS-84 ellipsoid.
computed.hdopRelative: This file's HDOP doesn't behave like standard HDOP, so its values are ranked within the track: each step holds a quarter of the fixes.
computed.shares: The share of the track's time spent in each step, from the times between fixes.
computed.steps: The steps are chosen from the shown tracks, so a color means the same value on each of them. They change when you show or hide a track.
computed.stepsEven: The shown tracks stay below running pace ({running}), so speed steps are equal parts of {top}: from standing still up to a round number at the top speed they usually reach.
computed.stepsLog: The shown tracks move faster than running pace ({running}), so speed steps are spaced on a log scale: each step reaches about {ratio} times as fast as the one before.

options.title: Options
google.street: Street View at the selected fix
google.myMapsHow: To see the track on Google: in My Maps, create a map, choose Import under its layer and pick your GPX file. This uploads the file to your Google account. NMEA and Columbus Fusion logs can't be imported there.
measure.accel.long: From the logger's motion sensor, which measures three axes (x, y, z) about 10 times a second. Each reading is the magnitude of that three-axis vector, √(x² + y² + z²), in g with gravity included, so it's about 1 g at rest. Each fix takes the strongest reading in its second; braking, turning and bumps push it above 1 g.
halo.hint.accel: Wider halo: harder push or jolt
note.motion: The logger's motion sensor recorded {n} readings a second. Pick Acceleration under Color or Halo to see them.
note.route: This file saves the recording as a GPX route, the form meant for planned paths, but every point has a time, so the app shows it as a track.
computed.accel: Worked out from the logger's motion sensor, which measures three axes (x, y, z) about 10 times a second: each reading is the magnitude of that vector, √(x² + y² + z²), with gravity left in (about 1 g at rest), and each fix shows the strongest reading in its second.
details.clockNote: This file's times have no time zone. Pick the zone the logger's clock was set to; the whole track moves with it.
details.speedUnitNote: This file doesn't say which unit its speeds are in. Pick the one the logger uses; every speed changes with it.
timeline.resetZoomHint: Zoom back out to the whole timeline (or double-click it). Scroll, or drag across the timeline, to zoom in.
inspect.asBoth: , shown as the line color and the halo
inspect.colorHere: The line's color at this point
inspect.haloHere: The halo's width at this point
google.myMapsShort: Import a GPX file there to see the track
inspect.medianHintEven: The median of this second's {n} readings (the upper of the two middle ones): {v}
inspect.peakHint: The strongest of this second's {n} readings: {v}. The map and the timeline color this second by it.

inspect.readingsSome: {shown} of the {n} readings in this second, from the lowest to the strongest, with the median and the strongest of them all highlighted

tracks.selectHint: Pick tracks to combine or remove
select.removeAgain: Click again to remove the selected tracks
combine.why.few: Select 2 or 3 tracks of the same trip to combine them.
combine.why.many: At most 3 tracks can be combined.
combine.why.combined: A combined track can't be combined again.
combine.zone: These tracks share little time. {file} doesn't say which time zone its clock is on: check its time zone, then combine.
combine.duplicate: These are the same recording twice: the same number of fixes over the same time, or the same fixes at the same moments. There's nothing to combine.
combine.apart: These may not be the same trip: they are over {distance} apart for most of the time they share. Check their time zones, or combine them anyway.
combine.full: Ten tracks are loaded, the most the app holds. Remove one to add a combined track.
combine.empty: These tracks have no moment in common to combine.
combine.tooLong: These tracks cover too much time to combine: about two weeks of fixes between them is the most. Combine shorter tracks of the trip.
combine.name: {ids} Combined Track
combine.shape: How much to trust each source
combine.shapeHint: Drag the handle toward a source to trust it more. Each source still counts by its own accuracy too.
combine.zeroOne: Source {k} is at 0%: it only fills gaps, where no other source has a fix.
combine.zeroTwo: Sources {a} and {b} are at 0%: they only fill gaps, where source {c} has no fix.
combine.eleLower: source {b} reads {m} lower than source {a} throughout
combine.eleHigher: source {b} reads {m} higher than source {a} throughout
details.logsNote: The combined track keeps its own copy of each source: changing or removing the tracks it came from doesn't change it.
details.clockFast: Source {k}'s clock read {s} s ahead of source {r}'s: its times were made {s} s earlier to match.
details.clockSlow: Source {k}'s clock read {s} s behind source {r}'s: its times were made {s} s later to match.
details.eleOffset: Source {b} reads a steady {m} {dir} than source {a}: one of them probably gives heights above the ellipsoid rather than above sea level. The combined elevation averages them as recorded, so where the sources giving it change, grade and climb aren't counted across.
computed.combinedSpeed: The weighted average of its sources' own speeds (each recorded, or worked out for that source alone), never from the combined fixes.
timeline.toPointHint: The fix picked on the map is outside the zoomed part of the timeline: center the timeline on it.

note.repeatsDropped.one: 1 fix that only repeated the position before it was dropped: this logger repeats its last position until it has a new one. The track goes straight across such stretches.
note.repeatsDropped.other: {n} fixes that only repeated the position before them were dropped: this logger repeats its last position until it has a new one. The track goes straight across such stretches.

note.repeatsLong.one: 1 stretch longer than 2 minutes counts as a gap.
note.repeatsLong.other: {n} stretches longer than 2 minutes count as gaps.

combine.fullTrust: Source {k} is at 100%: it's never left out, even where it disagrees with the others.
map.styleFailed: The basemap couldn't load, so the tracks are drawn on a plain background. Try another basemap under Options.
